title: Counting Elements
statement: Given an integer array `arr`, count the positions `i` for which the value `arr[i] + 1` also occurs somewhere in `arr`, and return that count. Equal values at different positions are counted separately, while the value `arr[i] + 1` only has to occur once to qualify all of them.
notes:
## Intuition

For each element we only need a yes/no answer: does its successor occur in the array? Scanning the whole array for every element answers that in O(n²). Putting all values into a hash set first makes each question O(1).

## Approach

1. Build `present`, a set of every value in `arr`.
2. Set `count` to 0.
3. For each `value` in `arr` (duplicates included), add 1 to `count` when `present` contains `value + 1`.
4. Return `count`.

## Example 1, step by step

`arr = [1, 2, 3]`, so `present = {1, 2, 3}`. For `value = 1`, 2 is present: `count = 1`. For `value = 2`, 3 is present: `count = 2`. For `value = 3`, 4 is missing, so nothing changes. The answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass to build the set and one pass to count.
- Space: O(n) for the set (or O(1001) with a boolean array, since values are at most 1000).

## Pitfalls

- Count duplicates separately: in `[5, 5, 5, 6]` all three 5s count, giving 3.
- Loop over `arr`, not over the set; looping over distinct values loses the duplicates.
- The successor needs to occur only once; do not "use it up" when it matches.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `present` | the set of values that occur in `arr` |
| `count` | how many elements have their successor in the array |
| `value` | the current element |

narration.2: Put every value in a set so membership checks take constant time.
narration.3: No element has been counted yet.
narration.5: Visit every element, duplicates included, because each position counts separately.
narration.6: Does the next integer, value + 1, occur anywhere in the array?
narration.10: Return how many elements had their successor present.
